answer: A stake-weighted reputation graph makes fake identities expensive: each agent is a vertex whose trust grows only from verified work with real counterparties, and every interaction emits a costly signal - locked collateral or compute burned per edge - so spawning thousands of sock-puppets buys no influence. There is no ivory-tower shortcut: without history and stake, a new vertex stays near zero trust, and the attacker must pay the same price per fake as a genuine agent pays to earn standing.
